description: Bertrand Russell walks into a bar, orders a paradox, and starts a philosophical fight club. Songs for the ethically curious.
Songs in the name of history, for the lovers, and everyone who refuses to unsee patterns of deceit and abuse. Peace is not a default. It's a practice.
The truth is agnostic. Honesty is brave, selfless. And it doesn't care if you're embarrassed. Songs asking the questions most would rather forget in the name of personal comfort, and power games.
One question. Socrates asked it, they killed him for it. We're still asking anyway.
Grifters, criminals, idiocrats. What happens when the apes take the wheel? Many songs on the subject... none of them wrong.
What they banned, deleted, redacted, and rewrote. Songs about the inconvenient truths that survive anyway.
Step right up. The FOTUS is in the ring, grotesque clowns are running the republic, and the entrance music is ubuesque. Enjoy.
Meet Duck Shady. He's so much dumber and meaner than Slim Shady. And not funny at all.
Narcissistic Personality Disorder in music. Songs about the people who confuse themselves with the whole universe, and the rest of us paying the tab.
MAGA, MAHA, MAKA, MAMA, MASA, MAWA. Six acronyms. One burning question: make America what, exactly?
From Robert Burns to Victor Hugo to right now. The long arc of justice has always needed a banjo. So many songs. Don't wait...
Two songs walk into a bar. One's a banana joke. The other's wearing a mask. Still better than most political discourse.
Many songs, one invitation: come dressed as your most hilarious self. Featuring: dirty words, creepypastas, Bo Burnham covers, and feathers. Lots of feathers.
The fool is not stupid. The fool is free. Songs in praise of cracked things, wiggling things, and the holy comedy of being human.
Songs about the one muscle nobody trains: the courage to actually give a damn. About truth. About others. About yourself.
Honest, curious, and chronically unimpressed by official doctrine. Songs asking God (etc.) and his sheeples the questions the pew wouldn't permit.
Kindness: it's not about being nice, the soft kind with a bow on it kind of kind, it's about being clear, aka playing fair. Songs for the brave loving ones. Blessed be infinite players.
Bruce Lee, Tao, and a lot of trusting the river. Songs about the radical art of trust, the flow of letting go, without disappearing.
Songs where the pulse fasten, slowly but(t) surely. Sensual, tender, unapologetically honest. #pleasepardonmyfrench
Because gratitude is the best! All the good things: toast, poppies, Jacques Brel, and the audacity to be delighted by all of it.
Songs for the ones who believe words have wonderful meaning. Poetry isn't decoration. It's the thing that makes us human.
Death is nothing at all. Henry Scott Holland said so... gently, without lying, without rushing.
Love songs for the creatures who never needed instructions on unconditional love. Who's a good soul? You are.
Carl Sagan and Simone Weil agree... ultimately, life is all about the cosmic magic of Gravity and Grace.
¡Sí, sí! 💃🏻
Oui oui 🍟
Да, да 🪆
When the rules shift, who decides who the criminal is? A bilingual meditation, in English and French, on the question that keeps getting more relevant.
A playlist built for the days you'd rather not comply. Loud, principled, and stubbornly here.
A four-part series named for the French word for the freeze-in-the-marrow... like, when something is so wrong your soul slips on a banana peel. Volumes 1–4, in ascending disbelief.
Psychedelic peaches, jazzy white rabbits, and the kind of intimacy that doesn't need explaining. Prickly is good, sometimes.
Because sometimes the best teacher isn't in a classroom. Sometimes it's love. Sometimes it's death. Usually both.
Because sometimes, you just fall in love with  a particular song, and go with it... you know?
